title: Plan a Memory Session
short: Put it all together: what to learn, which tool, how to recall, when to review, plus sleep and mixing.
trouble: Planning the encoding carefully and forgetting to schedule the reviews.

practice.q: Plan: a 13-year-old wants to learn the first ten elements of the periodic table, starting Monday the 2nd.
practice.a: A ten-spot palace, closed-book recall, reviews on the 3rd, 5th, 9th and 23rd.
steps: What: the first ten elements in order.
Tool: a memory palace with ten spots (age 12+, order matters).
Recall: walk the palace and write the list, then check.
Extras: mix the elements into review with other lists; teach a sibling.
practice.title: Worked example

blocks.html: You now know the whole system. A good plan answers five questions.

items: Which tool? The encode tool that fits the material and the learner's age.
How will I recall? Closed book: narration, blank page or flashcards.
When are the reviews? Days 1, 3, 7, 21 on the calendar, or a card in the box.
What else helps? Sleep, mixing old material into reviews, and teaching someone.
